sentences.text: Let’s climb it one rung at a time.
A sailing vessel underway keeps out of the way of three: a vessel not under command, a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver, and a vessel engaged in fishing.
So a sailboat gives way to a working trawler.
A vessel engaged in fishing, when underway, keeps out of the way of a vessel not under command and a vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver.
But listen to the wording: so far as possible.
Her gear limits what she can do, and the rule admits it.
And at the top sit the vessel not under command and the vessel restricted in her ability to maneuver.
Nobody is listed above them, because by definition they can’t easily get out of anyone’s way.
Remember the trick from lesson two?
Broken or busy sits at the top.
Then fishing, then sail, then power.
